SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Pollution? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water Pollution.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Pollution.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Pollution.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Pollution.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Classification of Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Classification of Plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Classification of Plants.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Classification of Plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Classification of Plants.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sound Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sound Energy.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Sound Energy.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sound Energy.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sound Energy.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing System.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Human Breathing System.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing System.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing System.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

13. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat transfer? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat transfer.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat transfer.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Heat transfer.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat transfer.

16. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----

21. In three clear sentences, explain Classification of Plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain The Human Breathing System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
